video_title: The Final Chapter of LeBron? 👑 Where Does He End His NBA Legacy?

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: John Ireland on Pistons' lack of consequences after blowout loss
quotes.excerpt: Detroit was so bad as recently as three, four years ago. I don't think they can do anything.

text_blocks.speaker: Lindsay
text_blocks.text: And you asked us something interesting in the pre-show meeting. Is there consequences for this for the Pistons?

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Yes. Normally there would be if you get blown out in a Game 7 at home and it's that lopsided. But Detroit was so bad as recently as three, four years ago. I don't think they can do anything.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: John Ireland suggests Kawhi Leonard or Kevin Durant for Pistons
quotes.excerpt: Here's two people they should go get: The first one is Kawhi Leonard. The other one is Kevin Durant.
quotes.quote: But if they don't go out and get a second scorer to help Cade Cunningham, they're just going to end the seasons this way for the foreseeable future. Here's two people they should go get. The first one is Kawhi Leonard because I think the Clippers would give him up and I think the Clippers need draft capital. The other one is Kevin Durant. But Durant's older than Kawhi. He's 37. But wouldn't those two guys, if they would have had Durant or Kawhi in this series, wouldn't they have won it?

quotes.speaker: Brandon Robinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Robinson on LeBron James potentially joining Giannis or the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Where he goes, LeBron could follow or join at the same time.
quotes.quote: Would a LeBron James and a Giannis Antetokounmpo pairing in Cleveland make sense? I would pay attention to Giannis quite a bit this summer because where he goes, LeBron could follow or join at the same time. But I also do think that LeBron's relationship with certain key members of the New York Knicks do make sense. William Wesley, who works in the front office of the New York Knicks, has known LeBron James since he was in high school. If you remember, William Wesley has been recruiting all his life. When John Calipari was fired as the head coach of the then New Jersey Nets, he was an assistant coach in Philadelphia under his mentor Larry Brown.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: John Ireland on salary cap issues for ECF losers pursuing LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: If you bring LeBron in, chances are you're going to have to get rid of one of your core components.

text_blocks.speaker: Lindsay
text_blocks.text: So I have a question. Does the loser of the Eastern Conference Finals believe that they are LeBron away from the Finals? Like Knicks or Cleveland. If they lose this series, do they go out and get LeBron?

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: The problem is that both of those teams are loaded with high salaries. So if you bring LeBron in even for that 15 million mid-level that Mace was talking about, chances are you're going to have to get rid of one of your core components. The Knicks would have to give up on somebody like Josh Hart or Mikal Bridges. There's already talk that the Cavaliers might have to move off of Jarrett Allen or Evan Mobley, but they were both great yesterday.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: John Ireland updates LeBron James's odds of staying with Lakers
quotes.excerpt: It makes the most sense for LeBron to come to the Lakers. They can pay him the most money.
quotes.quote: I'll say it again, it makes the most sense for LeBron to come to the Lakers. They can pay him the most money. He loves living in LA. But where there's smoke, there's fire. Dave McMenamin's report last week was accurate. If I had to up my percentages again, I would say now I'm looking, here I'll do it right now. LeBron, LA Lakers equals 49%. Other equals 49%. Retirement is 2%. So you are saying that there's as likely a chance that LeBron will play somewhere else as it is that he will play here. 49, 49.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Mason and John Ireland debate Lakers' future with or without LeBron James
quotes.excerpt: I think that it's time to build a roster for the future around Luka.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: If he can only get 15 out there, why should he make more money here?

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Because we can pay him, we can go over the cap.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: We can go over the cap, but at the same time, we've got to build a young, athletic roster with three and D wings.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Now you sound like the people that call Sports Graffiti.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: Wait, I'm not thinking about just 2026, 2027. I'm thinking about the next year and the year after that. And honestly, John, there are players out there that I think could make the difference.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Someone will call Sports Graffiti and say in essence what you just said, just cut bait now.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: I didn't say anything negative about LeBron except to say I think that it's time to build a roster for the future around Luka. I'm not crapping on LeBron.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: So you're on the Andy Kamenetzky position. Get rid of LeBron. Not because you don't like him, but because you want to move on to the next chapter.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: I want LeBron because he gives us a better chance to win next year.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Mason
text_blocks.text: I care about next year and the year after that. And honestly, John, there are players out there that I think could make the difference. But we'll talk about that on Sports Graffiti today.
